title: I Enforced the Hotel Pool Towel Card on the Guest Relations Lead

parts.text: I handed over a towel card at 11:02 a.m. and received one towel. The guest relations lead walked past with three and no card, saying staff demo. The sign said one towel per card, extra $25. I was forty-one, kid in floaties, holding a single rectangle of cotton. I photographed the sign, her stack, and my card. Then I asked the pool attendant to log a staff demo of three. At 11:08 she told the attendant I was harassing leadership in front of my kid, who asked why the lady had our towels.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: My kid is asking why leadership has three towels and we have one card.

social.video_title: Staff demo of three towels, one-card sign — Part 1/2
social.description: Floaties, $25 extra, a stack. The kid noticed. Would you have bought extras?

parts.text: Guest relations issued two more towels on a second card they should have used the first time. The log stayed. Demo became a training note. My kid swam. Cotton multiplied legally. Leadership still leads, with cards. Harassment is a word for a sign. I did not yell. I pointed. Pointing is how kids learn counting. The pool was wet on purpose. We returned all three on time so the $25 could stay theoretical.

social.video_title: The second card appeared after the kid counted — Part 2/2
social.description: Training note, legal cotton, on-time return. Was a demo a stack?
